description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of video content categories analyzed in the paper, showing how different genres contribute to the dataset used for training or evaluation. The chart is divided into twelve distinct slices, each labeled with a category name and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment is “People Blogs” at 17.2%, followed by “Entertainment” at 13.9% and “Howto Style” at 9.7%. Other notable slices include “Education” (8.7%), “Sports” (7.7%), “News Politics” (6.4%), “Science Technology” (6.4%), “Comedy” (5.6%), “Gaming” (4.6%), “Travel Events” (4.6%), “Film Animation” (4.6%), “Pets Animals” (4.3%), “Autos Vehicles” (4.8%), and “Music” (2.3%). Each slice is color-coded differently for distinction, and percentage values are printed directly within each segment. The chart includes a legend, though it is not visually present in the image provided, and all slices appear as standard wedges without any visual emphasis such as explosion or bolding. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order, starting from the top with “Howto Style,” and appear to be sorted in descending order of size, with “People Blogs” being the largest and “Music” the smallest.
